newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 30.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Football League last night cleared Essendon's Michael Prior of racially abusing Collingwood's Robbie Ahmat, however neither player was happy with the finding. Essendon believe Prior, while cleared, has not been freed completely with the stigma associated with the charges while Collingwood suggested the process in resolving racial vilification matters could be improved. Page 20.

An investigation was opened yesterday by the Australian Football League into an incident in which Hawthorn player Brendan Krummel allegedly received a poke in the eye - requiring an overnight stay in hospital - during Saturday's game against Sydney at Waverly Park. Krummel says he received the injury in the lead up to being head-butted by Sydney player Jason Mooney. Page 20.

North Melbourne Giants basketball team forward, American Mike Mitchell, has been arrested by New South Wales Police after being charged with an alleged assault occasioning actual bodily harm and common assault. The charges arise from an alleged incident outside a Sydney Kings Cross nightclub on April 20 involving two women. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian rugby union team the New South Wales Waratahs have made eight positional changes for their next Super 12 match after the team's devastating loss to the ACT. Phil Kearns has been rushed back after three weeks of inactivity while Matt Dixon has been plucked from the representative wilderness. Page 46.

Geoff Lawson is again fighting to retain his position as New South Wales cricket coach, with the State Cricket Board expected to elect the coach for 1997-98 within two weeks after the position was advertised early this month. Last season NSW won outright four games in 10 to finish level on 28 points with eventual Sheffield Shield winners Queensland. Page 45.

Australian retailer Gerry Harvey has bought into horse racing with his acquisition of the Magic Millions company two days ago for "around A$7 million". However it did not take Harvey long to sell half of the company to television identity John Singleton ad Bankers Trust managing director Rob Ferguson. The venture stages sales and the subsequent race for horses sold at the sales at its Queensland Gold Coast base. Page 45.
THE AGE

Australian Football League umpire Geoff Caulfield has tendered his resignation amid criticism of his performance in the round four Western Bulldogs versus Melbourne clash at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Caulfield has admitted that his decision to award a free-kick against Melbourne player Jim Stynes, which led to an easy goal for the Bulldogs, was wrong. Page B14.

Australian cyclist Kathy Watt looks likely to forgo a possible pursuit match against rival Lucy Tyler-Sharman at the August world track cycling championships in Perth to recover from hamstring injuries and concentrate on the road season. Page B12.

Australian basketball Melbourne Tiger general manager Barry Capuano said yesterday his team would not rule out taking legal action against the National Basketball League if they were penalised for playing Mark Bradtke without clearance last Friday. Bradtke returned last week from a one-season run with American team Philadelphia 76ers. Page B12.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian soccer team Heidelburg United be expelled from the Victorian Premier League after a shocking assault on referee Perry Muir during Heidelburg's 2-2 game against Bulleen on Monday night. Mur was verbally abused, spat on and hit by angry spectators as he tried to leave the field after the game. Page 70.

Australian Football League Carlton player Scott Camporeale is expected to be sidelined for at least a month after being diagnosed with glandular fever. Carlton football manager Colin Kinnear said Camporeale complained of feeling lethargic about a week ago Page 69.

The ninth Australian Junior Wheelchair games, also featuring competitors from America and New Zealand, ended in Ballarat this week with Victorian athletes showing a good result. Event director Shona Casey said this year's Games was the biggest yet, with 10 athletes competing. Page 63.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The decision to cut four clubs from the Sydney grade cricket competition next season has been rescinded by the New South Wales Cricket Association. The nine-member board initially voted to reduce the 20-team competition to 16. Petersham and Balmain are to merge, with Sydney University, University of NSW and Mosman teams relegated to shires competition. Page 70.

Australian Rugby League North Sydney coach Peter Louis was yesterday found guilty by the New South Wales Rugby League of "bringing the game into disrepute". Louis escaped a $A10,000 fine and was given stern warning by the board after referring to the touch judges during the mid-April Norths-Balmain game as "imbeciles". Page 69.

Australian basketball team Sydney Kings are currently in a tough position after starting the 1997 National Basketball League season down 1-3. A loss in this week's home and away series against the Townsville Suns and Brisbane Bullets could see the record drop to 1-5 - signalling even worse times for the team. Page 67.
